newsitem.title: TURKEY: Last month 50 unsolved murders in east-Turk MP.
newsitem.headline: Last month 50 unsolved murders in east-Turk MP.

text.p: A parliamentary deputy from Turkey's main opposition party said on Tuesday that about 50 people were murdered by unknown assailants over the past month in the southeast, where Turkish soldiers and Kurdish rebels are fighting.

"In the last month 50 have been killed by persons unknown," Sebgetullah Seydaoglu, a Motherland Party deputy from the southeastern city of Diyarbakir told parliament. He did not reveal the source of his information.

Human rights groups accuse the Turkish security forces of being behind scores of "mystery murders", mainly of Kurdish activists in southeast Turkey, where the army is battling a 12-year Kurdish insurgency.
The Ankara-based independent Human Rights Association said that around 3,500 people were killed by unknown assailants since the mid-1980s.
A technician for Batman Telekom, a southeastern phone company, and his seven-year-old son were found dead -- riddled with machine-gun fire -- at the side of a road in Batman province on Tuesday.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Turkish security forces and Kurdish rebels fighting for autonomy or independence in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
